question: A 45-year-old man with a history of biliary colic presents with one-day of intractable nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain radiating to the back. Temperature is 99.7 deg F (37.6 deg C), blood pressure is 102/78 mmHg, pulse is 112/min, and respirations are 22/min. On abdominal exam, he has involuntary guarding and tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant and epigastric regions. Laboratory studies show white blood cell count 18,200/uL, alkaline phosphatase 650 U/L, total bilirubin 2.5 mg/dL, amylase 500 U/L, and lipase 1160 U/L. Which of the patient's laboratory findings is associated with increased mortality?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lipase -> Acute pancreatitis -> Increased mortality -> 80% CHAIN: Amylase -> Acute pancreatitis -> Increased mortality -> 75% CHAIN: Total bilirubin -> Biliary obstruction -> Increased mortality -> 70% CHAIN: White blood cell count -> Infection or inflammation -> Increased mortality -> 60% CHAIN: Alkaline phosphatase -> Liver dysfunction -> Increased mortality -> 80%
enhanced_information: Elevated lipase levels are associated with increased mortality in acute pancreatitis. Amylase levels are also linked to mortality in this condition. Total bilirubin elevation is associated with biliary obstruction but not directly linked to increased mortality. White blood cell count elevation indicates infection or inflammation but is not as strongly associated with mortality in this context. Alkaline phosphatase elevation, indicating liver dysfunction, is also linked to increased mortality.
analysis: The patient's presentation is concerning for acute pancreatitis given the symptoms, physical exam findings, and significantly elevated amylase and lipase levels. Among the laboratory findings, elevated lipase levels are strongly associated with increased mortality in acute pancreatitis. While amylase levels are also linked to mortality in this condition, lipase is considered a more specific marker. Total bilirubin elevation is associated with biliary obstruction but not directly linked to increased mortality. White blood cell count elevation indicates infection or inflammation but is not as strongly associated with mortality in this context. Alkaline phosphatase elevation, indicating liver dysfunction, is also linked to increased mortality.
